items_missed: No agenda statement and no 'sound good?' confirmation — jumped straight from 'How can I help you?' into the quote
Never captured the customer's name or email — she deflected the email at minute 1 and he never circled back, so a hot, budget-qualified long-haul lead left the call with zero record in EMMA
Entire Clock section skipped: no 'clock starts on-site when the contract opens,' no 2.5-hour minimum, no 15-minute prorated increments
Entire Save Your Ass prep speech skipped — no 'prep before move day = shorter move = lower bill,' no consolidation examples, no 'take a carload' tip, on a purely hourly quote with 'a billion boxes'
No booking attempt — he had live inventory (5 trucks Sunday, 3 Monday) and still closed with 'all you have to do is call us back' instead of asking for the booking
No email handoff, no bolded-details recap, no 'reply with any corrections'
Never gave business hours or a direct way to reach him/us

Probe gaps: no box count (customer literally said 'a billion boxes' and he moved on), no garage/storage/balcony, no long-walk or narrow-hallway/tight-turn check, no parking or HOA/COI check at the apartment, no 'anything you're worried about?' stressor question
Said 'we would have to stay overnight' on the San Antonio → Waxahachie haul but never priced or explained what the overnight costs the customer

Quoted a 2-mover team for a 1,300 sqft 3-bedroom plus a very large box count, loading to a 2nd-floor apartment with no elevator — likely under-scoped, and no walk-distance question was asked to check it
No school-bus/equivalents framing to help her picture truck size or time
top_strength: Genuinely excellent differentiator and consultative work in the middle of the call — he nailed the No Worries $2,000 coverage against the 60¢/lb state baseline, made clear it is built into the rate with no deposits or cancellation fees, and then proactively armed her with the exact hidden-fee questions to ask his competitors. He also volunteered the cheaper load/unload-only structure and the cheaper Sunday/Monday rates unprompted, which is why she ended the call saying he was 'number one.'
coaching_note: He earned the business and then didn't ask for it. She told him he was in the lead and deciding by Wednesday, he had five trucks open on Sunday in front of him, and his close was 'all you have to do is call us back' — with no name, no email, and no profile built, so there is nothing to follow up on and no way to win her back if competitor #4 calls first. Coaching rep: when a customer deflects the email up front, don't drop it — quote first, then re-ask at the end ('I'll put this in writing so you have the numbers side by side when you compare'), and always make one direct booking ask with the availability you just quoted.
phone_presence_notes: Warm, easy, non-pushy energy that the customer explicitly rewarded — she volunteered that he was the most helpful rep she'd spoken to and ranked him number one — though he never used her name and the call carried a lot of false starts and repeated filler.
